Hon'ble Surendra Singh-I,J.
Heard Sri V.P. Singh Kashyap, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Sunil Kumar Tripathi, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
None appears on behalf of the respondent no. 2.

The present criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against the order dated 10.11.2022 passed by Special Judge, (POCSO Act), Kasganj, whereby the learned Judge has rejected the Bail Application No. 1782 of 2022 (Bhupendra Vs. State of U.P.) moved on behalf of the appellant in Case Crime No.
93 of 2022 under Sections 376, 506 I.P.C. & Section 3(2)(V) of S.C./S.T. (P.A.) Act, Police Station- Sunnagarhi, District- Kasganj.

sentences.text: According to prosecution case, informant, Kunwerpal Valmiki lodged first information report on 08.09.2022 by submitting written report to the effect that her two grand-daughters aged 19 and 17 years had gone to cut grass in the field.
Appellant and co-accused, Jeeshan, often used to tease them and tried to outrage their modesty.
When the informant made complaint, they threatened him with country-made pistol that they will forcibly kidnap his grand-daughters from the house.

After Bhupendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199229446/
1 investigation, on the basis of the statements of victim recorded u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the case was converted to one u/s 376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(V) S.C./S.T. Act.

sentences.text: In case he is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
He has submitted that the victim has supported the prosecution case in her statements recorded u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
However, he could not dispute the aforesaid factum of the case as argued by the learned counsel for the appellant.

Considering the submissions made on behalf of the learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.G.A., facts and circumstances of the case, statements of the informant/victim u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and that of other witnesses u/s 161 Cr.P.C., medical report of the victim, fact that the case was initially registered u/s 354, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(1)? and 3(1)? of S.C./S.T. (P.A.) Act and after statement of victim was recorded 21 days after the incident, Section 376 I.P.C. was added to the case crime number, period of incarceration undergone by the appellant and the fact that appellant has no criminal history to his credit but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
Accordingly, the appeal is hereby allowed.
The impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is hereby set aside.

Let the appellant, Bhupendra, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
Bhupendra vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199229446/
2 (i) That the appellant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless his presence is exempted by the court.
(ii) That the appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the appellant shall not involve in any criminal activity.

It is also made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The trial court/J.J.Board shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusion on the basis of evidence led, uninfluenced by any finding or observation whatsoever in this order.
